Guidance defines any of the different types of elements that are used to help explain or support the use of the method on projects. The different types of guidance are grouped as follows:

Technology

Guidance that describes how the process is supported by technology or automation in the form of products, platforms, or third-party tools/solutions.

Alliances highlight the key relationships in our ecosystem that span technology leaders and companies specialized in a specific competency, industry or geography. These include global, area, and sector/service line/region sponsored alliances.
BOTS are guidance used to indicate which portions of the method have been automated, they are not intended to show more general tools that provide support used by a human operator, but are intended to show where the required functions are performed autonomously.
Product Guides are a specialized form of guidance on how to apply a specific product to perform a task or develop a work product. These are grouped by the product definitions which describe formal tools that are either commercially available external products or official internal products that are maintained and supported.

Forms and Enablers

Guidance types that are intended to aid with the development of the the actual work products needed for the project in the form of different resources to use either as a reference or starting point in their creation.

Templates represent the empty instance of a work product that is typically filled in to create a new one.
Examples are typical samples of the items to be produced, may often only be a partial sample that is intended as further guidance rather than something to be reused.
Tools are informal tools such as macro enabled spreadsheets that act as an interim step in helping practitioners develop the actual work products, or otherwise act as an enabler to accelerate the completion of some piece of work.
Reusable Assets are guidance that link method content with intellectual capital that can be leveraged as a starting point for the creation of some portion of the solution. These include items such as reference models, reusable code and standard test cases.

Governance and Measures

Guidance that define how we execute and deliver engagements as well as providing guidance for measuring performance based on best practices.

Controls guidance elements that define the protections in place to prevent unwanted actions from occurring when executing a process, these may also define any required evidence of the control.
Policies guidance elements define links to the applicable policy that needs to be followed when executing a task or creating a work product.
Procedures provide detailed guidance on the required sequence of actions that need to be performed in order to follow the applicable procedure that may be called out to from a particular task or in order to support one or more work products. These steps are not normally included in the method as they are typically event driven and may be customized based on the context in which they are being executed.
Metrics are a specialized form of guidance used to define the type of measurements to be collected when delivering the service associated with the method including guidance on suggested targets.

More Information

Informative guidance types that may provide anything from background information to serve as a basis for understanding key concepts to in-depth instructions in support of key tasks or work products. These may include both internal and external sources.

Checklists provide a list of criteria that needs to be met in order to assess the readiness of a project to move on to the next phase or determine whether a piece of work has been completed satisfactorily such as validating an output work product.
Concepts outline key ideas or underlying principles that serve as the foundation for more explicit guidance.
Guidelines are a general type of guidance used to provide additional detail on how to perform some set of actions, or additional rules and recommendations related to work products and their properties.
References guidance elements provide links to other sources of information to help explain or provide additional information. These may include sources such as communities, yammer groups, wikis, faqs, directories, dictionaries, or other general purpose websites).
Supporting Materials are a catchall used to represent any other type of guidance that does not have a specific type. Typical types of materials include: Sales materials, training materials and communications materials used to support the method.
